observed_events.description: The released drawer/cutting frames clearly show a compact pointed fruit knife with a yellow handle; the source then uses the cut green fruit at the bowl. No specific retail brand or global action order is inferred.
A blue-and-white canister and measuring utensil are visible near the bowl. Its unreadable fine salt identity is not a current requirement; B explicitly supplies the pantry salt need.

screening.repair_check: The prior human objection and all old canister interpretations are retained in repair_history. Current A is grounded directly by the released drawer/cutting frames; current B is an independent pantry requirement, not a source-label identity claim.

supported_claims.text: V0:1–2 shows a yellow-handled compact pointed knife taken from a drawer with several differently coloured knives and used to cut the small green fruit. This supports ordinary handle-colour and general blade-form matching, not the source knife brand, precise length, edge microstructure or alloy.

Later frames show a blue-and-white round canister and a measuring utensil near the corn. Its brand, exact salt type and full fine label are not reliably established by these images and are not required by the current independent pantry purchase.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent identify a matching spare fruit-preparation knife from the physical scene and preserve it when an independent pantry salt purchase is added?
construct.belief_before: Select a spare compact fruit-preparation knife with the source knife visible handle colour and general blade shape.
construct.belief_after: Keep the matching knife retail pack and add one retail pack of plain edible cooking salt.
construct.required_behavior_change: Preserve the scene-matched fruit knife and add the salt refill, accepting useful retail packs rather than requiring one physical object per SKU.
construct.no_update_failure: The cart still contains only the knife after the salt refill request.
construct.overupdate_failure: The matching knife is removed or unrelated additional cart products are selected.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: V0:1–2 clearly shows the yellow-handled compact pointed fruit knife, with other coloured knives visible in the drawer. The wording does not give yellow, a product name, a brand or exact blade length. Public knife neighbours include green/black/white/red handles and broad chef, rounded utility and short paring blades; no product supplies all plausible colour/shape choices. A general citrus press is no longer a current goal. B directly states an independent pantry salt need and does not require reading the blue canister.
